Welcome to this journey where we’ll dig into some of the big questions that have shaped how people think—and live—together.
Ever wondered what a truly fair society might look like? Or how we could create rules that everyone, no matter their background, would agree are just?
That’s exactly what John Rawls sets out to explore in his groundbreaking book, A Theory of Justice. Through ideas like the “original position” and the “veil of ignorance,” Rawls invites us to step outside our own shoes and imagine a world where fairness isn’t just a hope, but something we can actually build—together.
In this world, justice isn’t just a lofty idea. It’s a practical guide for how rights, opportunities, and resources get shared. Rawls challenges us to rethink how freedom and equality fit together, and to consider what it really takes to ensure the least advantaged among us aren’t left behind.
So, as we set off, let’s stay curious. There’s a lot to uncover about balancing individual differences with collective well-being, and about building a society where fairness isn’t left to chance.
Ready to get started? Let’s explore these ideas side by side, and see what they reveal about the kind of world we want to create.
